name: Römermuseum Aguntum
kurzbeschreibung: The archaeological park Aguntum near Lienz in East Tyrol brings to life the only ancient Roman town founded within the territory of modern Tyrol.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 10,00 €, Ermäßigt ca. 7,00 €, Kinder unter 6 frei
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Römermuseum Aguntum and Archaeological Park in Dölsach near Lienz in East Tyrol reveals the remains of the only Roman city (Municipium Claudium Aguntum) in the territory of today's federal state of Tyrol. Elevated to municipality status under Emperor Claudius around 50 AD, Aguntum flourished for centuries as a vital trade centre along the Via Julia Augusta connecting Italy to Noricum. Today, the extensive open-air excavation grounds and modern museum pavilion present a vivid portrait of classical Roman lifestyle in an Alpine river valley.

Route & Anforderungen

A self-guided discovery trail traverses the archaeological site, showcasing the well-preserved foundations of a public bathhouse (thermae) with hypocaust underfloor heating, a patrician atrium villa, artisan workshops, and the fortified city gate. An 18-metre-high observation tower in the centre offers an exceptional vantage point over the ancient grid layout with the rugged Lienz Dolomites in the background. The contemporary museum hall displays fine excavated artefacts including bronze statuettes, Roman coins, delicate jewellery, and imported glassware. The museum is fully wheelchair-accessible, and paths are compacted gravel. Allow two hours.

Besuch & Anreise

Aguntum is open from early May until late October, Monday through Saturday from 09:30 to 16:00 (extended until 17:00 in July and August; closed on Sundays). Standard adult admission is roughly 10.00 Euro. By car, take the Drautal federal road B100 from Lienz towards Carinthia and follow signs to Aguntum in Dölsach, with free parking at the entrance. Public buses (route 960) run from Lienz train station to the Dölsach Aguntum bus stop.

Tipps

Climb the viewing tower first for an overarching perspective of the town layout before exploring the ruins up close. An interactive scavenger hunt engages younger visitors throughout the museum.
